title: Merge-Time Regeneration of Shared Generated Files: Eliminate index, backlog and ledger Conflicts Between Parallel Branches
target_platform: git worktrees / merge workflow; backlog index, chronicle ledger, cognitive ledger and events log
hypothesis: A merge-prep step that regenerates the shared generated files from their sources (index.jsonl and backlog.md from the mission manifests, the chronicle ledger from the entries, the cognitive-ledger aggregate from events.jsonl) and treats the append-only logs with a union merge lets 100% of 60 two-branch merges that both rewrite these files complete with zero manual conflict resolution, with every regenerated file byte-identical to a from-scratch regeneration, and it reports (not silently repairs) any aggregate that does not equal what its events imply.
falsification_criteria: Any of the 60 merges needs a manual resolution or leaves a regenerated file different from a from-scratch regeneration; or an aggregate that disagrees with its events is silently adjusted instead of reported; or merge-prep takes longer than 2 s per merge; or it modifies a file outside the declared shared-generated set.
baseline_evidence: MISSION-031: `index.jsonl` conflicted in 60 of 60 real two-branch merges because every mission regenerates it (flagged by the board, not eliminated). Real incidents on 2026-11-03/04: index.jsonl and backlog.md collided on every mission PR; agy's MISSION-024 score existed only as an uncommitted edit to the cognitive-ledger aggregate while its events.jsonl entry was never committed, so the aggregate could not be rebuilt from events and had to be reconciled by hand.

model_routing.frontier_escalation_condition: Escalate only if ledger semantics require judgement about which of two conflicting scores is authoritative.

related_missions.MISSION-031: SPAWNED BY: found the 60/60 index.jsonl conflict boundary.
related_missions.MISSION-033: FEEDS: the orchestrator runs merge-prep when it merges workers' PRs in order.

projected_impact.basis: Declared 2026-11-04 by claude-code from the hypothesis; confirm with `manage_coordination.py verify`.
